sections.content:
65,920 people

were counted on the census as "education managers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Education managers plan, organise, direct and co-ordinate the administration, support systems and activities that facilitate the effective running of a school, university, college or other educational establishment.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "education managers", 17.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "education managers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.title: The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years
sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "education managers" included:

  • health services and public health managers and directors
  • registered specialist nurses
  • production managers and directors in mining and energy

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "education managers" there were more women than men (73.9% compared with 26.1%).

This means "education managers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "teaching and other educational professionals".

Men made up 26.1% and women made up 73.9% of "education managers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "education managers" included:

  • registered mental health nurses
  • physiotherapists
  • cleaning and housekeeping managers and supervisors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "education managers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "education managers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "education managers", 9.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (84% compared with 16%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (95.5%) than self-employed (4.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
